thread:
nightdash-bot: ALERT: nightly: model-runtime-serving P95 latency +18% vs baseline over the last 12h. Regression window starts ~2025-11-18T02:10:00Z. See dashboard: https://nightdash.internal/redwood/runtime/p95

maya: saw the alert, thanks. Is this across all regions?

aj: looking now — initial query shows spike concentrated on us-west-2 but small uptick eu-west too.

sophie: I pulled the perf job: `perf-ci/2543` had a failing regression (P95 +22%). Link: https://ci.internal/builds/2543

ci-bot: perf-ci/2543: test-suite=nightly-perf, job=runtime-p95, status=regression, baseline=176.3ms, current=215.8ms

leo: timeline: two merges landed between last green nightly and this one: PR#4227 "kernel-selector: prefer stable kernels for short seq" and PR#4231 "kv: more aggressive eviction for small prefixes"

maya: hmm kernel-selector change was flagged in code review but merged to unblock model A throughput. Could be related.

aj: quick local bisect: reverted PR#4227 on staging -> reran perf harness -> P95 back to 170ms. Reapplied PR#4231 only -> P95 stayed ~214ms. So signal points to kernel-selector change.

sophie: can you paste the exact commands you used?

aj: sure — bisect steps:
```
git checkout main~3
git cherry-pick <commit-before-4227>
# apply all commits except 4227
./tools/perf/run_nightly.sh --suite runtime-p95 --target us-west-2
# sample output
# P95 170.4ms (no 4227)
```

aj: also profiled some samples with perf-map: kernel selector picked matmul_kernel_v2 for short seq lengths ~64, which is slower on our tensor cores than matmul_kernel_v1. Profiling dump:
```
[profile] mem-bound: 42%
[profile] matmul_kernel_v2: 38% CPU time, avg latency 2.9ms
[profile] matmul_kernel_v1: 12% CPU time, avg latency 1.1ms
```

leo: interesting — the selector heuristic bumped short seqs to v2. Did the heuristic change threshold?

maya: PR notes: it favored more numerically-stable kernels for sequences <128 to reduce fp error. That explains the stability rationale, but perf hit is bad for production.

selma: the perf test matrix uses seq distribution skewed to short sequences; this change would show up there first.

aj: agree. My local run indicates revert fixes P95. I propose a revert PR for 4227 as hotfix, and then we iterate on a smarter selector fallback policy (only use v2 for sequences that actually trigger instability).

sophie: +1 for revert. Any risk to correctness from revert?

maya: revert removes the stability preference; numerical error regression is small on our smoke tests, but we should run targeted numerical evals before merging revert.

ci-bot: note: we also saw increased KV eviction churn in logs for the same window but AJ's bisect suggests it is downstream causality, not root cause.

aj: kv churn was probably amplified by higher per-request latency -> longer active KV lifetimes -> slightly more evictions. So it's secondary.

leo: plan: 1) AJ to open revert PR for 4227 and include the perf traces in the description. 2) Run numerical eval suite against revert branch. 3) Create follow-up PR to adjust selector to only pick v2 when numeric delta > threshold (and add canary). 4) Roll out revert to canary hosts once CI passes.

aj: creating PR now: https://git.internal/redwood/runtime/pull/4279 (WIP) — includes perf logs and profiling output.

sophie: I'll queue a canary job after the revert passes CI. Also let's add a short-term alert to Nightdash to monitor P50/P95 and KV eviction rate during rollout.

maya: assign oncall to watch: @leo you want to own the canary watch?

leo: taking it. Will monitor dashboards for 6h after deploy.

selma: we should also add a regression test to perf-ci that validates kernel selection doesn't flip for short-seq baseline models without explicit numeric instability flags. Filed issue: https://issues.internal/infra/1892

aj: FYI I ran a smoke numeric-check diff between main and revert: max L2 diff ~3e-6 across 1k examples. I'll upload more detailed evals in the PR.

maya: thanks everyone. Moving to action. If anything else shows up ping here. :rotating_light:
